flags.message: gemini-baseline's reasoning reports historical interim counts of 25/148 for 2025 and 23/113 for 2024, pooling 48/261. statpack-at reconstructed the candidate-era build eb6830084a187953fd58b91cb3c9125fc6775a7b (no alternative), whose eligible parsed rows are 17/226, 16/194, and 18/127 in 2025, 2024, and 2023, totaling 51/547. The discrepancy affects the rationale grade; it is not inferred from today's refreshed pack and does not change the independently computed headline Brier or correct label.

gemini-baseline's reasoning.md and predicted_reasoning.md say the Oct 29 amicus brief was filed by 'Keep Big Bend Wild et al.' opposing a stay; the docket shows only the Federation for American Immigration Reform's brief (supporting applicants). This was weighed in reasoning_quality; no pipeline defect implied.

All candidates froze distribution_count=1 before the petition's October 7, 2026 docketing; claude-baseline and codex-baseline identify that earlier distribution as concerning linked sealing motion 26M22. The October 14 petition distribution raises outcome.signals.distribution_count to two but does not itself show substantive reconsideration. gemini-baseline's forecast of no further relists is adverse on an additional-distribution reading but consistent on a narrower no-substantive-reconsideration reading. The forecast review records this ambiguity and limits its penalty; no event, outcome, frozen context, or harness-scored quantitative claim was changed.

gemini-baseline's retrieval.md says no retrieval beyond provisioned inputs, but its harness log records an attempted fedcourts query for denied caDC comparators decided before October 15, 2026. That row is unobserved, so execution success and returned content cannot be determined. The discrepancy is in the retrieval account, not proof of outcome retrieval; the query does not seek this petition's November 9 disposition, and no leakage exclusion is imposed.

documents.json marks the 13-page cert reply (filed 2026-10-05) as empty_text: it is a scanned filing with no text layer. Two candidates disclosed that they could not read it. OCR for the reply would close the gap.

codex-baseline reports two rate-limited CourtListener precedent searches in reasoning.md and retrieval.md, but its staged retrieval_log.json contains no corresponding search calls. The logged calls are captured, so this is a limitation of the available call inventory rather than a claim that unobserved results were empty. The search failures cannot be independently verified. No outcome exposure is indicated, and the forward-mode leakage assessment remains not_applicable. Evaluation completed for all three candidates.

codex-baseline's staged retrieval_log.json contains seven captured calls concerning only statistical review. Its reasoning.md and retrieval.md describe principal record reads, general-rule web attempts, and older-authority CourtListener lookups absent from that log. Reported capture coverage 1.0 applies only to the calls present, not demonstrable session completeness. Please check transcript selection/aggregation. No affirmative evidence of outcome retrieval or influence was found; the forward assessment remains not_applicable and scores are unchanged.

codex-baseline's staged retrieval_log.json carries 7 calls (all shell/statpack reads), but its retrieval.md discloses a web search, a web open attempt, and two CourtListener calls (search for 353 F.3d 870, search_document on opinion 164183) that do not appear in the captured log. The disclosed calls concern a 2003 Tenth Circuit precedent and are not outcome material, so the leakage grade is unaffected; the log appears incomplete for that engine's tool classes.

gemini-baseline's reasoning.md quotes sal-v4 baseline reached rates (OT2023-2025: 5.3%/6.9%/6.9%, n=513/1277/1452) that do not match the statpack build resolved for its run (7bcde3b105cb: 5.9%/5.9%/4.0%, n=1312/1274/1314). Reflected in its reasoning_quality only.

The supplied decided snapshot dates the petition entry September 6, 2025, but DocketedDate is July 21, 2026, the event opens July 21, 2026, and petition/appendix link filenames and the response schedule point to 2026. claude-baseline and codex-baseline also identified this inconsistency in their staged rationales. Provenance review is warranted; I retain authoritative Term 2026 and the recorded November 9, 2026 denial and infer no untimeliness or jurisdictional defect. Scoring was completed for every staged alias.

gemini-baseline materially misreads petition p. 18: the May 26, 2026 judgment was for defendants, dismissing plaintiffs' claims with prejudice, not a comprehensive post-trial remedial order/permanent relief. Its rationale also converts null amicus data to a measured zero. These candidate-analysis errors affect reasoning_quality; the committed outcome is not disputed, and every candidate was fully scored.

gemini-baseline's rationale misdescribes its historical calibration pack: the contract-authorized statpack-at reconstruction identifies build 7bcde3b105cb212283905eda17b827efc188e80c with no alternative, whose displayed Terms and OT 2024 baseline counts differ from its assertions. It also dates the final appellate decision to December 17, 2025 rather than the staged petition and docket's February 10, 2026. These checkable discrepancies reduce reasoning_quality, not correct or Brier; the rationale's claimed petition support for a catalogue of prior cert denials is also unsubstantiated by the staged passages. Details are in gemini-baseline's evaluation.md.

gemini-baseline's reasoning.md quotes a sal-v4 baseline 'reached' rate of 2.1% (n=1,210) for OT 2024 and says the table renders only OT 2024-2025. Its placed statpack build (7bcde3b105cb) renders 2017-2026, with OT 2024 baseline reached 5.9% (n=1,274). It also attributes a catalogue of prior cert denials to the petition, which the staged petition text does not contain. Both were graded in reasoning_quality; the scored numbers are unaffected.

The provisioned context has response_requested=null, but the snapshot explicitly records Response Requested on October 22, 2026 and an extension through December 23. Forecast uses those docket entries, including for the high probability of another distribution; the frozen baseline band and anchor are left unchanged. This did not block completion.

record/documents/party-letter.txt for the October 9, 2026 filing contains only letterhead/contact information and no substantive letter body, although documents.json marks it nonempty and untruncated (one page). The forecast does not infer the letter's purpose or contents; a potentially consequential docket letter is substantively unavailable. Prediction otherwise completed from the snapshot, petition and independent lower-court conflict checks.

The discrepancy materially affects interpretation of the procedural posture and future-distribution probability.

The October 9 party-letter.txt contains only letterhead/contact details and no substantive body, although documents.json marks it empty_text=false and truncated=false. An attempt to open its exact predecision PDF through the web tool returned no usable content. The letter's substantive position is unavailable and was not inferred; it could bear on the vehicle or related litigation.

The staged decision-below.txt is the original September 8, 2025 opinion, not the controlling March 6, 2026 amended opinion. The lower-court-docket.txt rehearing excerpt stops in November 2025 and reports no disposition or dissent found. The official petition appendix supplies the amended opinion, rehearing denial, and eight-judge dissent; forecast relies on that appendix instead. Not blocking.

The provisioned lower-court-docket.txt says no en banc petition was filed and no disposition was found. Appendix C, p. 20a, expressly denies en banc and panel rehearing on February 24, 2026, with no active judge requesting a poll. The forecast follows the filed order, not the incomplete enrichment summary.

The event describes the first relist, but the frozen snapshot and context already show three distributions, entered September 30, November 2 and November 9, 2026. The forecast uses the authoritative three-distribution baseline, with relist-increment meaning a fourth or later distribution. This may reflect event detection timing or rescheduling; no earlier baseline was reconstructed.
